terms.text: The edge line of a shape: where one thing ends and another begins. The outside contour is also called the silhouette.
The outside shape of something, as if it were filled in solid black.
Simple shapes such as circles, ovals and boxes that you draw lightly first, to set size and position before adding details.
How big parts are compared with each other, for example how wide something is compared with how tall.
Things farther away look smaller, and parallel lines seem to come together in the distance.
How light or dark an area is, from white paper to the darkest pencil mark. Color doesn't matter for value.
Adding values (light and dark) so a flat drawing looks solid and three-dimensional.
Shading with sets of crossing parallel lines. More layers of lines make a darker area.
The brightest spot where light hits a surface directly. Usually left as clean paper.
The empty space around and between objects. Drawing these gaps is a great way to check shapes.
